drive: Autopilot. The recording drives on from here.
story: This rescue rover is driven from far away. Its operator must never lose the link.
Off the cable and straight onto Wi-Fi, without a moment offline.
A normal rover without CONTINUA drives this same road at the same moment. Its status is beside ours, at the top.
Ahead, a cutting blocks Wi-Fi and cellular. CONTINUA's road map saw it 79 m out and is warming up satellite.
The banks close in: Wi-Fi and cellular fade out.
CONTINUA is on satellite and still connected. The normal rover has lost its link.
CONTINUA is on satellite and still connected, though its video pauses on the thinner link. The normal rover has lost its link.
Wi-Fi and cellular are gone. CONTINUA is on satellite and still connected, though its video pauses on the thinner link.
Through the cutting, CONTINUA never lost its link. The normal rover was cut off for 4.5 s and had to stop.

The same road, 20 times. CONTINUA with its road map kept the link 20 times out of 20; the normal rover, 0. Keeping every network on also stayed connected, at about 3× the cost - and, with big uploads held back, for less than CONTINUA.
